items.title: Exercise 1.7: justify the noncompact log-Sobolev test

source.anchor: Section 2.1.1, printed pp. 48–49 / PDF pp. 60–61; compact-test LSI and density extension; consumer Exercise 1.7, printed p. 43 / PDF p. 55
source.attribution: Chewi states the compact smooth test inequality and refers to density for extension. The explicit analytic domain and proof below are an original sufficient ASTIS reconstruction, not a quoted theorem or the maximal closed form domain.

items.statement: Starting with function-form LSI on compact smooth tests, retain its constant on smooth tests with square-integrable function and genuine gradient and integrable square-log-square. In a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space the radial cutoff products are valid compact smooth tests. With those same three integrability conditions, the cutoff integral limits hold for C2 functions in a complete real Hilbert space without finite dimension or a finite-measure assumption.
assumptions: The source reference is a probability on a finite-dimensional Euclidean carrier. The Lean extension assumes the compact smooth inequality with fixed coefficient 2C; on arbitrary Borel measures this premise uses totalized Bochner integrals, whereas the source probability case has genuine compact-test integrals.
The extended test is smooth, with f and its genuine gradient in L2 and f^2 log(f^2) in L1. Its sign and total square mass are unrestricted.

The cutoff-limit prerequisite retains all three analytic inputs: f and its genuine gradient in L2, and f^2 log(f^2) in L1. It lowers the regularity requirement to C2 and uses a complete real Hilbert/Borel carrier without probability, local finiteness or finite dimension.

obligations.label: Actual dominated mass, entropy-integrand and gradient-energy limits
Same coefficient on the noncompact smooth analytic domain

bindings.boundary: An extracted measure-generic cutoff proof, previously private in GaussianLogSobolev. This is not additional cutoff mathematics, an LSI statement, or a claim of compactness in infinite dimension.

assumption_deltas.source: The source leaves the extension from compact smooth Euclidean tests to density arguments.
assumption_deltas.lean: Three radial cutoff limits for C2 f with f and gradient in L2 and f^2 log(f^2) in L1 on a complete real Hilbert/Borel space with an arbitrary measure.
assumption_deltas.reason: These are explicit sufficient analytic inputs for the shared approximation. Finite dimension is used for compactness only at the actual inequality consumer; the limits do not need it.

bindings.boundary: A sufficient smooth-domain extension. For arbitrary Borel measures the compact premise is a statement using Mathlib's totalized Bochner integrals; it is not a claim that classical entropy is defined on every compact smooth test. The actual cutoff tests used in the proof have genuine integrable terms. This is not the full closed Dirichlet-form domain, the Poincare conclusion, or a new assumption on the final compact PI theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The source starts with the compact C-infinity function-form inequality with coefficient 2C.
assumption_deltas.lean: The premise is the same compact smooth test class and the same coefficient, without requiring a stronger compact C2 premise.
assumption_deltas.reason: Every actual cutoff approximant of the smooth input satisfies the given smooth compact premise.

assumption_deltas.source: Extension to appropriate test functions is attributed to density.
assumption_deltas.lean: Explicit smooth L2 function, L2 true gradient and L1 entropy-integrand domain on an arbitrary measure in finite dimension.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is one sufficient domain. The square-root perturbation application proves its membership separately; the whole weak/form domain is not claimed.

assumption_deltas.source: The source works with a probability law, so continuous compact tests and their continuous compactly supported gradients have genuine integrals.
assumption_deltas.lean: The measure is arbitrary Borel. The all-compact-tests premise is expressed using totalized Bochner integrals, which are zero on nonintegrable terms.
assumption_deltas.reason: Compact support alone is not an integrability guarantee for an arbitrary measure. The proof tests only actual cutoff products with integrable mass, entropy integrand and energy, as established by the envelopes in the shared proof. The classical source specialization is on probability measures; no equivalence with an undefined entropy on general measures is asserted.
